name: Lego Voxel
basis: why: a brick mosaic is 'a palette problem' of fixed brick colours; how: one stud per cell, nearest brick colour, studs drawn as plastic cylinders
note: A toy medium; kept apart from tesserae mosaic setting because its units are fixed and gridded.

lumenary.blurb: A mosaic of plastic bricks: every cell is one brick colour with a round stud on top.

facts.bestOn: Bold, colourful subjects and simple faces

why: A brick mosaic is a palette problem. Each stud can only be one of the colours that bricks come in, so the picture is rebuilt from a small, fixed set. A little ordered dithering lets a smooth gradient become a mix of two neighbouring brick colours, and the drawn studs with their shadows and shine make it feel like plastic.
how: Reduce the picture to one pixel per stud, each the average of its patch.
Add a small offset from a 4 × 4 Bayer pattern so gradients mix two brick colours.
Replace each stud with the nearest brick colour, using a weighting that favours red in bright colours and blue in dark ones.
Draw each stud as a short cylinder with a shadow, a darker side, a lighter top and a pale arc of shine.
Give each brick a light top and left edge and a dark bottom and right edge.
history: The LEGO brick in its modern interlocking form was patented in 1958 in Denmark. Mosaics from plates of single-colour studs became a hobby of their own, and LEGO later sold sets that build art from them. A voxel is a pixel with volume, and games such as Minecraft turned the idea of a world made of cubes into mainstream culture.
terms: The round bump on top of a brick.
A pixel in three dimensions: a small cube in a grid.
Mixing nearby colours in a regular pattern to suggest shades between them.
paragraphs: The picture is reduced to one pixel per stud, so a stud is an average of its patch. A brick has one of a fixed set of real brick colours, so each stud takes the nearest colour in the set. Distance between colours uses a weighting that gives the red channel more weight when the colours are bright and the blue more when they are dark, which is closer to how colours look than a plain distance. Before the nearest colour is found, a small offset from a 4 × 4 Bayer pattern is added, so that smooth gradients become a mixture of two brick colours instead of one hard step.
Each stud is a short cylinder drawn with a shadow, a darker side, a lighter top and a pale arc of shine. The brick under it gets a light top and left edge and dark bottom and right edge.

equations.tex: d^2=\Big(2+\frac{\bar r}{256}\Big)\Delta R^2+4\,\Delta G^2+\Big(2+\frac{255-\bar r}{256}\Big)\Delta B^2,\qquad \bar r=\frac{R_1+R_2}{2}

equations.note: The side of the stud is drawn at 74% of the brick colour and the top at 107%.

presets.text: Fewer studs make a chunkier, more readable mosaic.
The greys palette gives a smooth sculptural portrait.
Switch the shine off for matte bricks.
